name: Deep Ecology
summary: Deep ecology holds that human and nonhuman life have value in themselves, and that the present industrial, growth-driven civilization has pushed interference with nature to a critical level. It calls for a deep change in economic, technological and ideological structures, favoring quality of life over a rising standard of living, a gradual fall in human population, local autonomy and non-exploitative relations between groups. It is a philosophy and platform more than a party program, so it says little on most conventional political questions.
scope: The Naess line of the deep ecology movement: Arne Naess's 1973 'shallow and deep' contrast and the eight-point platform drawn up by Naess and George Sessions (published by Devall and Sessions, 1985), with Earth First! style direct action as a close ally. It is a philosophy rather than a political program, so answers on questions it does not address are low-confidence inferences from its principles. It excludes social ecology, ecofeminism and eco-authoritarian readings.

sources.usedFor: Direct action, nonviolence, bioregionalism, green party realists and fundamentalists.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Naess's anti-class posture opposes exploitation between groups, but the platform says nothing on health care; a modest yes is inferred from that egalitarian stance.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Deep ecology is silent on wage law and its focus on quality of life over standard of living gives no clear direction.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The movement opposes capitalism and growth-driven economics and holds that reform within the market system cannot halt the crisis, though it is not a pro-planning position either.

public-ownership.rationale: Adherents prefer local autonomy and self-sufficiency over large central bodies, so state ownership of big utilities does not fit neatly; the texts do not address it.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Opposition to class exploitation and to affluence-focused politics suggests sympathy, inferred rather than stated.

unions-good.rationale: The platform never addresses labor unions; anti-class stance and green-left alliances pull one way, hostility to industrial work structures the other.

property-fundamental.rationale: Giving nature value apart from human use implies owners have no absolute right to destroy it; inferred from the intrinsic-value thesis.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Deep ecologists blame industrial capitalism for the ecological crisis and want its structures changed, so tighter regulation is the least they would accept.

cut-welfare.rationale: Not addressed directly; the anti-exploitation stance and rejection of affluence-driven politics make welfare cuts unlikely to be favored.

worker-ownership.rationale: The movement favors local self-governance but has no stated view on firm ownership; this is a question about economic organization it leaves open.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Preference for local autonomy and small-scale, non-authoritarian technics (Mumford) suggests distrust of state surveillance, though the texts do not address it.

legalize-drugs.rationale: No stated position; adherents appear divided between libertarian and communitarian leanings.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The movement has no stated view on speech law.

strong-leader.rationale: Decentralization and local autonomy run against concentrating power in a strong leader, an inference rather than an explicit statement.

state-harmful.rationale: Strands tied to green anarchism say yes, while the platform itself calls for policy change, which presumes some state; adherents are split.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun law is not discussed in the platform, and adherents hold no common view.

empower-police-military.rationale: Anti-class, anti-domination stance and skepticism of large hierarchical structures suggest opposition, inferred.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: The movement has no position on sex work.

decide-locally.rationale: Naess lists local autonomy and decentralization as a defining point, favoring local self-government and fewer links in decision chains.

rehabilitation.rationale: Criminal justice is outside the movement's concerns.

traditional-family.rationale: No stated position; not part of the platform.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The movement does not address marriage law; adherents are mixed.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed in the platform; though adherents favor population decline, they have not tied this to abortion law.

more-religion-public.rationale: Naess drew on spiritual sources but the movement is pluralist about philosophical foundations and does not seek public religion; inferred.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Not addressed; anti-exploitation stance suggests sympathy but the movement's focus is non-human.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Naess favors diversity of cultures, but the movement has no stated view on national traditions as such.

gradual-change.rationale: Deep ecologists hold that interference has reached a critical level and that economic and ideological structures must change fundamentally, not by gradual reform.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Naess is documented as suggesting immigration restriction alongside gradual population decline, though this is contested among adherents.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Local autonomy and fewer decision links far from the people argue against stronger remote bodies; inferred.

free-trade.rationale: Naess warns that vulnerability grows with influences from afar and favors local self-sufficiency, which cuts against global free trade.

nation-first.rationale: Self-sufficiency favors localism, yet the platform seeks global ecological action; no clear nationalist position.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The platform does not discuss war or intervention for human rights.

open-borders.rationale: Naess's reported immigration restrictionism points against open borders, though this is a contested corner of the literature.

limit-growth.rationale: Point seven prefers quality of life over a rising standard of living, and the movement opposes economic growth as a threat to the biosphere.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Adherents hold that human interference has reached critical levels and call for sweeping structural change; climate is a clear application though the platform predates it.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Deep ecologists reject technology as morally neutral and hold that authoritarian technics should be abandoned, not relied upon to fix the crisis.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Deep ecologists cite nuclear weapons as a case of non-neutral technology, and large-scale, centralized technics are what they want abandoned.

revolution-justified.rationale: Earth First! used direct action and the platform obliges members to act, but the movement's committed activists pledged nonviolence and no revolution is stated.

experts-over-public.rationale: Preference for local autonomy and critique of the expert-led industrial system suggest skepticism of technocracy; inferred.

central-planning.rationale: Naess favors decentralization and local self-government, which fits poorly with central planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: The movement does not discuss ownership forms.

land-value-tax.rationale: Tax design is not addressed, though a land tax could fit ecological goals.

tax-inheritance.rationale: No stated view; the anti-class posture suggests mild sympathy, but not enough to call.

basic-income.rationale: Not addressed; quality-of-life emphasis might favor it but the sources are silent.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Self-sufficiency favors local production, but protecting industry is not an aim of the movement and industrial growth is opposed.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Directing investment toward strategic industries serves growth, which deep ecology opposes.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Local self-sufficiency and small-scale technics fit dispersed ownership, inferred.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Adherents want economic structures changed but the platform does not call for abolishing money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: No stated position on monetary institutions.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Statist bodies setting wages and prices are a centralizing structure at odds with local autonomy; not addressed directly.

one-party-rule.rationale: Naess's platform says nothing on party systems; opposition is inferred from his stress on local autonomy.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: The movement takes no position on forms of government.

democracy-best.rationale: Green thinkers link sustainability with community democracy, but deep ecologists have not endorsed democracy regardless of ecological outcome.

direct-votes.rationale: Bioregionalists influenced by the movement favor grassroots political arrangements, a mild fit with direct participation.

workers-councils.rationale: Council-based power is a question of class politics that the platform never takes up; its decentralism fits loosely but supports no firm answer.

right-to-secede.rationale: Local autonomy and decentralization imply regions governing themselves, inferred.

natural-rulers.rationale: The ecocentric view precludes accepting authority based on status, and the anti-class posture rejects natural hierarchy.

political-violence-never.rationale: Activists pledged nonviolent direct action, yet Earth First! faced charges of tree spiking, so adherents are split.

war-builds-character.rationale: War is destructive of life, and the movement values live-and-let-live; inferred.

separate-church-state.rationale: Church-state relations are outside the platform, which is explicitly open to religious and secular foundations alike.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: The platform is deliberately pluralist across religious and philosophical grounds and does not rest on scripture.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Rejects capitalist market solutions; no stated view on courts.

military-superiority.rationale: Domination between nations is opposed by the anti-class posture, which extends to developed versus developing nations.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Naess favors diversity of cultures but rejects domination; the sources do not address national ethnic composition.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Naess has an anti-class posture against exploitation, but deep ecologists locate the root of crisis in industrial civilization and not in class conflict as history's engine.

equal-outcomes.rationale: The platform concerns relations between humans and nature, not distributive equality among people.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Deep ecologists cite indigenous societies as sustaining their lands for millennia, which supports their stewardship, though no formal claim is stated.

colonial-reparations.rationale: The movement does not address reparations.

civilizational-union.rationale: Decentralization and local autonomy argue against large civilizational blocs; inferred.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Naess's relational view of the self rejects atomistic individualism and extends self-realization through identification with nature.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Point eight puts an obligation on adherents, but the movement has no stated priority of duty over rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: The first platform point and the SEP entry make intrinsic value of human and nonhuman life, independent of human use, the core tenet.

limit-population.rationale: Point four says flourishing is compatible with substantial population decline; adherents favor gradual reduction but reject coercive or apocalyptic methods.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Adherents blame industrial civilization for damage that threatens collapse and possibly extinction, stating this repeatedly.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Rejecting technology as neutral and calling for abandoning authoritarian technics means speeding technological change is opposed.

human-enhancement.rationale: Naess favors soft technique and a relational self rooted in nature; enhancement is not addressed so this is inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Large, authoritarian technics are rejected and local autonomy is preferred; inferred.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Digital privacy is not an issue the movement's texts take up.

restore-past-order.rationale: Deep ecologists admire pre-industrial and indigenous cultures but their aim is a new ecological order, not restoration of a social one.

results-over-ideology.rationale: The platform holds that attitudes and value structures must change, not just policy outcomes; adherents treat the worldview as primary.

direct-action.rationale: Naess chained himself to rocks at Mardalsfossen and Earth First! embraced direct action, though green parties also participated in elections.

means-match-ends.rationale: Naess favors nonviolent action but no explicit statement links means to ends.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Deep ecologists admire primal cultures, but most blame industrial civilisation rather than agriculture and do not call for foraging; adherents differ.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: Naess favors division of labour but not fragmentation of labour, so he keeps the division and rejects only its fragmenting form.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Distribution among humans is not discussed; the vital-needs idea in point three concerns limits on harming nature, not a distributive rule.

production-for-use.rationale: Opposition to growth-driven capitalism and the emphasis on vital needs imply production for need, though the platform does not frame it this way.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The anti-class posture opposes exploitation but deep ecology does not adopt the Marxist account of profit.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from Naess's anti-class and local-autonomy principles.

collective-farming.rationale: Local self-sufficiency fits small farming; compulsory collectivization is not supported.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Adherents blame capitalism for ecological damage but have no stated thesis about war between powers.

taxation-theft.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's call for structural policy change presumes legitimate public action.

harm-principle.rationale: Giving moral standing to nonhuman life expands the harms the state may restrict beyond harms to humans; inferred.

individual-rights-only.rationale: Naess's relational view treats organisms as knots in a net, rejecting atomism and recognizing value in species and ecosystems.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; militarism conflicts with live-and-let-live.

exit-over-voice.rationale: The movement's texts say nothing on how to compare exit and voting as checks on government.

state-as-business.rationale: Treating citizens as customers applies market logic, which the movement opposes as part of the industrial-capitalist system.

positive-liberty.rationale: The movement has no stated theory of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: Claims about who holds power in universities and media are not part of deep ecology's concerns.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Naess favors equal right to live and diversity; the movement says nothing on racial ability differences.

organic-representation.rationale: Bioregionalists favor grassroots arrangements, but corporatist representation is not stated.

total-state.rationale: Not discussed in the platform; inferred from Naess's local autonomy and decentralisation.

national-rebirth.rationale: Not addressed; the movement's desired change is ecological, not national.

territorial-expansion.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from Naess's anti-class, anti-domination stance.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Not addressed; hierarchical authority conflicts with the anti-class posture.

bound-labor.rationale: Not discussed in the platform; inferred from Naess's anti-class posture.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Deep ecologists reject the idea of technology as neutral, but have no general thesis about knowledge and power.

universal-morality.rationale: Naess treated biospherical egalitarianism as an intuited axiom but the platform is deliberately pluralist about philosophical foundations.

single-common-good.rationale: Not addressed; the platform allows differing foundations.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The movement does not address diaspora citizenship, and its reported immigration restrictionism pulls against it while diversity of cultures pulls toward it.

revive-national-language.rationale: Naess values cultural diversity but takes no position on state language policy.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Local autonomy and anti-hierarchy suggest sympathy, inferred.

school-vouchers.rationale: Education finance is outside the movement's texts.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Deficit stimulus aims at growth, which adherents oppose; the position is inferred.

economic-freedom.rationale: The movement opposes capitalism and its growth imperatives and so does not treat economic freedom as essential.

rule-by-example.rationale: The platform proposes no theory of how rulers should govern.

national-self-determination.rationale: Local autonomy and diversity of cultures favor self-governing peoples; inferred.

force-without-un.rationale: Militarism conflicts with the live-and-let-live principle; not addressed.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Naess grounded the view in intuition and relational self-realization, not reason alone, and the platform admits religious foundations.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: The anti-class posture extends to conflicts between nations, so welfare exclusion does not fit; inferred.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Work conditions on welfare are not addressed by the movement's texts.

class-collaboration.rationale: The anti-class posture opposes exploitation but not in the form of class struggle; no stated view.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Naess values diversity of cultures and ways of life; inferred.

dominated-front.rationale: Naess opposes domination of developing by developed nations but no front is proposed.

workers-nation.rationale: Whether workers organize nationally or internationally is not something the platform takes up.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Anti-class, anti-domination principles imply rejecting legal role distinctions; not addressed directly.

ban-interest.rationale: No stated position, though critique of growth economies could point to either answer.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the egalitarian, anti-class principles.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The movement opposes class domination but has no stated theory of the state.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Expanding fossil fuel extraction drives the interference with nature that deep ecologists see as already critical.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Naess favors diversity of cultures, but the sources do not discuss assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy thesis about immigration finds no support in the movement's texts, which treat industrial civilization as the cause.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; green parties generally favor it but the platform does not.

national-mission.rationale: Imposing one's form of government on others contradicts the diversity of cultures and live-and-let-live principle.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Ecofeminists criticize deep ecology, and the movement has no stated view on this.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Not addressed; the movement criticizes structures rather than elites.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Adherents reject coercive or genocidal population solutions and stress intrinsic value of all life.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Transitional justice is outside the movement's concerns.

night-watchman-state.rationale: The platform calls for policy and economic structures to change, which a minimal state would not do.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; a guess from the movement's egalitarian principles.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Biospherical egalitarianism extends equal right to live to all life, humans included, though Naess noted it holds in principle only.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: The movement's sources do not classify states by their origin.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law questions are outside the movement's concerns.

restrict-conversion.rationale: The movement is pluralist on religion and favors diversity; inferred.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Biospheric egalitarianism is against needless killing but the movement permits killing for vital needs and has no cattle-specific policy.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Religious instruction in schools is not discussed; the platform is pluralist about religious foundations.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Strengthening state power conflicts with decentralization.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Local self-government and decentralization favor consent, inferred.

trade-surplus.rationale: Export-led growth runs against self-sufficiency and the movement's opposition to growth.

population-transfer.rationale: Adherents reject coercive population solutions and extend the equal right to live to all.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Not addressed as an absolute; the movement allows some killing for vital needs.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Naess ranks the live-and-let-live principle above the either-you-or-me struggle, rejecting competition as the key to flourishing.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Party bans are outside the platform, which proposes no constitutional doctrine.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Anti-domination appears in the anti-class posture but the movement has no theory of freedom.

separated-powers.rationale: The texts favor local autonomy but give no view on checks between branches of government.

vanguard-party.rationale: Hierarchical party leadership conflicts with local autonomy and anti-class principles.

priority-to-poor.rationale: The anti-class posture opposes exploitation, including between developed and developing countries; inferred.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Housing tenure policy is outside the movement's texts.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: Direct action is part of the movement; limits on picketing would be disfavored.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Adherents favor population decline but do not claim it is the main cause of poverty.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Naess favors diversity of cultures and ways of life; inferred.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Selection of officials is not addressed, though participatory politics might be sympathetic.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not addressed; domination by the state conflicts with local autonomy.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Price policy in scarcity is not a question the movement's texts address.

party-controls-media.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from decentralisation and local autonomy.

party-commands-army.rationale: Not addressed; opposition to centralized power suggests no.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Reported restrictionism by Naess fits, but this is a contested point among adherents.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: Pay of officials is not covered by the platform.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Fundamentalist greens rejected cooperation with other parties, but discipline in parties is not addressed.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Naess warns of vulnerability from distant influences, favoring local decision making over supranational bodies.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Concentrated executive power conflicts with decentralization.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is outside the movement's concerns.

clerical-rule.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from local autonomy and the platform's pluralism about religious foundations.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: Revolutionary defeatism is not a position the movement's texts discuss.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Diversity of ways of life is valued; inferred.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Not addressed; opposed concentration of power suggests no.

recall-officials.rationale: Grassroots, participatory democracy favored by bioregionalists makes recall consistent; inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Self-sufficiency and anti-militarism suggest yes but no stated position.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; coercive abolition conflicts with decentralized choice.

people-in-arms.rationale: Military organization is not discussed in the movement's texts.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Deep ecologists admire small, nature-embedded communities and blame industrial civilization, but the movement does not state this as morality.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National reunification is not addressed by the movement, whose preference for local autonomy gives no clear direction.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The movement's texts say nothing about the educated as a social group.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Naess favors diversity of cultures and ways of life, and live and let live, but did not claim cultural relativism as such.

death-penalty.rationale: Extending moral value to all life, human life included, suggests opposition; no stated position.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: School curriculum on sex and gender is outside the platform.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: The movement draws on ecology as science and has no ties to creationism.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Obscenity law is not within the movement's texts.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: Not addressed apart from reported immigration restrictionism.

minority-language-support.rationale: Naess favors diversity of cultures; inferred.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions from general law are not addressed by the platform.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Support for diversity of ways of life and non-conformity to industrial culture; inferred.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: The anti-class posture applies to developing versus developed nations; inferred.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: National independence movements are not a subject of the platform, so no stated position exists.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The movement opposes economic growth as an aim, so restricting freedoms to secure it would be rejected.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: The anti-class posture opposes exploitation of developing by developed countries; the platform calls for no aid program.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: Deep ecologists cite nuclear weapons as inherently destructive technology.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Executive selection is outside the movement's texts.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Monetary governance is not addressed, though the movement opposes growth-oriented economics generally.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: Live-and-let-live and anti-domination suggest willingness to compromise; inferred.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Intrinsic value of nature limits owners' rights; inferred.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: The characterization of the USSR is a Marxist dispute that deep ecology texts do not enter.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Platform point five says human interference with nature is already excessive and worsening, which favours acting early; the platform does not name the precautionary principle, so this is inferred.

collective-defense.rationale: Alliance doctrine is not discussed in the movement's texts.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: The movement's texts do not address the law of occupation.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Church-state power is outside the platform.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The role of the head of state is not discussed.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Local autonomy and decentralization oppose coercing regions; inferred.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Local autonomy and diversity favor regional self-rule within a larger union; inferred.

sacred-ruler.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the anti-domination principles.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; the anti-class posture suggests progressive taxation.

character-from-environment.rationale: Naess sees the self as relational and expandable through identification, but has no theory of upbringing.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from local autonomy and the anti-domination stance.

space-expansion.rationale: Expanding human reach is another form of interference and growth; the movement favors quality of life over expansion.

mixed-constitution.rationale: The classical theory of mixed government is not taken up by the movement.

leader-cult.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from the anti-hierarchical principles.

equal-parenting.rationale: Family-court policy is outside the movement's texts.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Deep ecology is not organised around class conflict or socialist state-building; inferred from its focus on ecological, not class, divisions.

land-redistribution.rationale: The platform says nothing on land tenure; redistribution to farmers could help or harm wild areas, so it is neutral.

refugee-return.rationale: Outside the platform; no principled position can be inferred.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: Inferred from its call for non-exploitative relations between groups and for local autonomy rather than state expansion.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: Inferred from the platform's emphasis on diversity and non-coercion; it is not a topic it addresses.

women-must-cover.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to domination; the platform does not address dress codes.

common-currency.rationale: Inferred from its preference for local autonomy and decentralisation over large integrated economic structures.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: Inferred from its local autonomy and decentralisation emphasis, which cuts against large supranational unions.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Inferred from its stress on cultural diversity and local autonomy.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Outside the platform; deep ecology's bioregional emphasis on staying in place is balanced by its general indifference to this question.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: Deep ecology calls for a change in ideology and values as well as economic structures, so it does not see change as driven mainly by production.

ban-cartels.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to concentrated, growth-driven industrial power.

no-bailouts.rationale: Outside the platform; adherents might oppose propping up growth-driven firms but have no stated position.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: Inferred: protecting nonhuman life requires constraints on what majorities may choose, so institutional limits are welcome.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: The platform does not address representation; adherents are split.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Inferred from its call for local self-reliance and a smaller economic footprint, though it rejects colonies and does not prescribe autarky.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Inferred: environmental standards fit its ecological aims, but many adherents distrust trade expansion itself.

moral-incentives.rationale: Its preference for quality of life over a rising standard of living implies reducing reliance on material incentives.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Naess advocated nonviolence, and Earth First! style direct action targets property rather than seeking armed revolution.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to domination and its egalitarian orientation among humans.

history-own-civilization.rationale: Deep ecology is silent on school history; Naess favours local autonomy but also biospherical egalitarianism. Genuinely indeterminate, inferred.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Naess's platform asks for non-exploitative relations between groups and local autonomy, which rule out rule over others for their improvement. Inferred.

patriotic-education.rationale: Loyalty is owed to the biosphere and local community, not national symbols; the texts do not address schooling, so inferred.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: The platform is silent on racial preferences; Naess's anti-class, anti-exploitation posture gives no clear direction.

public-money-creation.rationale: No stated position on money or banking; the platform calls for changed economic structures without specifying monetary ones.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Deep ecology holds that industrial growth economies push interference with nature to a critical level, implying they cannot continue indefinitely. Inferred; not framed as collapse theory.

former-empire-influence.rationale: Opposes domination between groups and favours local autonomy; imperial-style influence is not endorsed. Inferred.

delink-world-market.rationale: The platform favours local autonomy and self-reliance over growth-driven global industrial economies. Inferred; not addressed in terms of poor countries.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Naess takes an anti-class posture and the platform does not analyse worker exploitation; indifferent.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Biospherical egalitarianism and opposition to exploitation suggest disfavour of discrimination, but the platform is silent on property and association law. Inferred.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: A value platform with no program on constitutional design; adherents range from green parties to anarchists.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Inferred from Naess's call for non-exploitative relations between groups and local autonomy.

elective-rulers.rationale: Inferred from its anti-class, anti-domination stance; the platform does not address monarchy.

minority-veto.rationale: Inferred from its stress on deep change guided by principle; a single-member veto would block it, though local autonomy is valued.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: Naess supported nonviolent civil disobedience and the platform's last point obliges adherents to act for change; inferred for lawless rulers.

parliament-supreme.rationale: The platform is indifferent to the form of government, so no answer is inferred.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: The platform holds that nonhuman life has value in itself, independent of its use to humans.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Inferred from intrinsic value of nonhuman life and the claim that human interference is excessive; humane use is not endorsed.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Inferred from Naess's anti-class and anti-exploitation posture.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The platform obliges adherents to try to implement change, so withdrawal is disfavoured, though simple living is valued.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Inferred from its critique of consumerist, growth-driven civilization.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Inferred from its structural critique of industrial society's ideology.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Inferred from its opposition to exploitation between nations and groups.

native-born-offices.rationale: Inferred from its anti-class, anti-exclusion stance.

party-own-road.rationale: The platform is a philosophy and does not address party relations.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Inferred from the platform's local autonomy and decentralisation.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Inferred from its pacifist-leaning ethos and nonviolence.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Deep ecologists often admire indigenous ways of life, but political leadership over settlers is not addressed.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Inferred from its nonviolent, anti-domination values.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: Naess opposed violence and domination of all kinds, but adherents do not address the comparison.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Inferred from its egalitarian, anti-domination values.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: Inferred from the egalitarian stance of the platform.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from its nonviolent egalitarian ethos.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: Inferred from its respect for diversity of cultures and local autonomy.

paid-care-work.rationale: Inferred from its valuing of non-commodity life and quality of life over output.

filial-duty.rationale: The platform is silent on family obligation; inferred as neutral.

office-by-exam.rationale: The platform is silent on how officials are chosen; inferred as neutral.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Naess favours local autonomy but the platform is silent on foreign ownership; inferred as neutral.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The platform is silent on marriage law; inferred as neutral.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Naess's stress on local autonomy and decentralisation suggests accountability close to the community; inferred.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Inferred from the platform's opposition to growth-driven economic structures; it does not address pensions.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Inferred from the view that nonhuman life has value in itself and land should not be exploited as a mere resource; the platform does not address tenure.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: The platform is silent on institutional design; inferred as neutral.

single-official-language.rationale: Naess backs local cultural autonomy and diversity; inferred from that.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Naess favours local autonomy but the platform does not address foreign ownership; inferred as neutral.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: The platform opposes class exploitation between groups but does not address discrimination law; inferred as neutral.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: The platform calls for quality of life over a rising standard of living and a change in economic structures that drive consumption.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Inferred from the Naess line's commitment to non-violence and non-exploitative relations between groups.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Inferred from the stress on local autonomy and non-violent relations between groups; the platform does not address blocs.

corporate-influence.rationale: Naess criticises industrial, growth-driven structures; corporate capture of policy is an inferred extension, not a stated plank.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: The platform is silent on sovereignty and NGO funding; local autonomy and global ecological concern pull in opposite directions.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Platform point 4 calls for a substantial decrease in human population, so subsidising births runs against it.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local autonomy and place-based communities are favoured; limits on outside buyers are inferred from that, not stated.

job-guarantee.rationale: Deep ecology prefers quality of life over growth and has no stated view on employment programmes.

democratic-peace.rationale: The platform does not address democracy promotion or war between states; nothing in it settles the question.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Earth First! style direct action and civil disobedience are accepted allies, implying obedience is not owed when law permits ecological harm.

non-intervention.rationale: Ecological harm crosses borders, so adherents are unlikely to accept an absolute bar on outside pressure; this is inferred.

industrial-unions.rationale: Union structure is outside the platform, which is critical of industrial society itself.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Its call for non-exploitative relations between groups is incompatible with scapegoating a minority; inferred from that principle.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Family law is not addressed by the platform and adherents have no common line.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Informed public participation in ecological decisions is inferred to need open government information.

local-production.rationale: Local autonomy and decentralisation are part of Naess's summary of the movement, and industrial-scale global trade is what it criticises.

informal-organisation.rationale: The movement is non-hierarchical and favours direct action by small groups, though Naess also worked with parties.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not addressed; global ecological agreements and local autonomy pull in different directions.

religious-nation.rationale: Its universal view of value in all life does not define community by creed; inferred from that stance.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Naess's anti-class posture and opposition to exploitation between groups imply equality among peoples; inferred.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Local autonomy and bioregionalism imply communities keep their resources; inferred.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: The platform does not address property regimes, so this is left open.

defeat-communism.rationale: The platform takes no position on communism as a rival system.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: The platform is silent on how public services are delivered.

religion-illusion.rationale: Naess's spiritual, relational view of the self treats religious or spiritual experience as lasting, not a mere consolation; inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The platform holds that industrial, growth-driven civilization has pushed interference with nature to a critical level, so it is not seen as a foundation for a better society.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: The platform does not address gender or economic change.

socialized-care.rationale: The platform says nothing on domestic and care work.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Cultural diversity is valued, but language purging is not addressed; a mild no is inferred from that.

treaties-binding.rationale: Diversity, local autonomy and non-exploitative relations between groups imply respect for agreements with internal nations; inferred.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Local autonomy and bioregional decentralization favor small self-governing communities, though common property is not specified.

majority-settlement.rationale: Respect for local autonomy and cultural diversity implies opposition to steering settlement; inferred.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Naess's platform rejects the industrial growth paradigm shared by capitalism and communism, so a different course is implied.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Inferred: deep ecology's bioregional attachment to place and respect for Indigenous peoples pull one way, while its focus on nature rather than peoples' claims pulls the other.

holocaust-denial.rationale: The sources never mention the Holocaust; rejection is assumed.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Inferred from the platform's respect for diversity and absence of any moral policing of adult private life; its adherents overwhelmingly oppose criminalisation.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Inferred from the movement's grassroots, nonviolent stress on democracy; a few strands accept eco-authoritarian ideas, so the answer is not stronger.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: Inferred: deep ecology is often spiritual, but it has no program for state enforcement of religion and favours pluralism.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Inferred from the platform's opposition to exploitation; the movement rarely addresses colonial rule directly.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Inferred: the platform says nothing on religious war duties, and its adherents favour nonviolence and plural traditions.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: Inferred: the platform has no theory of religious legitimacy and favours nonviolent change.

participatory-democracy.rationale: Inferred from the platform's emphasis on grassroots, local decision making and bioregional communities.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Inferred: Naess's platform concerns humans and nature, not oppression categories, and adherents are split on social analysis.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Inferred: the platform is silent on the issue and adherents are split.

assisted-dying.rationale: Inferred: the platform says nothing on it, and adherents are split between autonomy and reverence for life.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Naess and Green movements often describe themselves as neither left nor right, but beyond the old axis.

alienated-labor.rationale: Inferred: the platform criticises consumerism and the loss of quality of life more than alienated labour as such.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Inferred: the platform's respect for diversity of cultures weighs against the claim, but it never addresses it.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: Inferred: some adherents are spiritual, but the platform places value in nature, not divine political authority.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Inferred: the platform is silent and adherents have no common view.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Inferred: the platform is silent on workplace law and adherents have no common view.

social-market-economy.rationale: Inferred: the platform calls for basic changes in economic structures, not social protection for growth economies.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Inferred: the platform is silent on armed forces and adherents focus on nonviolence in movements.

rich-first.rationale: Inferred from the platform's rejection of growth as the road to wellbeing and its focus on equity.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Inferred: the platform is silent on alliances and adherents have no common view.

dynastic-succession.rationale: The platform is silent; inferred from its opposition to exploitative relations between groups and its call for local autonomy.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: The platform does not address credit; its local-autonomy stance favors community finance but nothing is stated.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Silent on public finance; local autonomy would favor national choice, but nothing is stated.

property-franchise.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Naess's opposition to class domination and exploitation between groups.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Deep ecology is split here: some adherents link the domination of women and of nature, while others reject that framing as anthropocentric. The platform is silent.

reification.rationale: The platform makes no claim about capitalist social relations; its critique is of the industrial growth society and its ideology.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Silent on media ownership; inferred nothing definite from its focus on ecological values.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the call for non-exploitative relations, which fixed and public law serves.

racial-franchise.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Naess's call for non-exploitative, non-dominating relations between human groups.

online-participation.rationale: The platform does not address political technology; local autonomy favors face-to-face life, but adherents are split.

open-government-data.rationale: Not addressed; a modest yes is inferred from the call for deep change in political structures and accountability.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the platform's opposition to domination between groups and its respect for diversity.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Naess's opposition to exploitation and domination between human groups.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Deep ecology favours local autonomy and decentralised, grassroots decision-making, so assemblies of ordinary people suit it; the platform does not mention sortition, so this is inferred.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: The platform calls for deep change in ideological structures, and the movement draws on reinterpreted spiritual traditions rather than fixed doctrine; inferred from that stance.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; the platform is anti-class and focused on the biosphere, so it takes no clear stance on wealth and liberty.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Not addressed by the platform, and adherents ranging from antimilitarist to libertarian have no common view.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Not addressed; deep ecology often has spiritual or reverential attitudes toward nature, so promoting unbelief is unlikely.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not addressed; the platform is a philosophy without a stance on policing.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Not addressed; the platform's stress on local autonomy gives no clear guidance.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Not addressed; local autonomy and community favour community help, while the platform has no welfare position.

term-limits.rationale: The sources do not address this issue, so the answer is inferred from the general principles and adherents are split.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not addressed; local autonomy is valued but no particular voting mechanism is.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Inferred as split: the platform calls the situation critical, but its concern is the biosphere's diversity rather than human extinction, and it favours a falling human population.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: The sources do not address this issue, so the answer is inferred from the general principles and adherents are split.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: The sources do not address this issue, so the answer is inferred from the general principles and adherents are split.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: The platform says nothing on voting rights; its local-autonomy point gives no answer on residents' votes.

rent-control.rationale: The platform says nothing on housing; adherents have no collective position.

abolish-ip.rationale: The platform says nothing on intellectual property; adherents have no collective position.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Inferred from Naess's opposition to exploitation between groups and the movement's decentralist, non-militarist stance.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not stated in the platform; inferred from the call for deep change away from a destructive industrial civilization.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Not addressed in the platform; inferred from the call for local autonomy and non-exploitative relations between groups.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed in the platform; inferred from the call for non-exploitative relations between groups.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Not addressed in the platform; inferred from Naess's anti-class posture and preference for quality of life over wealth.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed in the platform; inferred from the inclusive ethic of valuing all life, though Earth First! style allies accept direct action.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Not addressed in the platform; inferred from the stress on human membership in the wider biotic community over national identity.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed in the platform; deep ecology has no position on this feminist-theory question.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed in the platform; deep ecology has no position on this feminist-theory question.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the platform's non-anthropocentric values, which do not centre national sacrifice.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Not stated; inferred because the platform is a philosophical value position, not a good-versus-evil spiritual war, though it is sometimes called spiritual.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Not addressed in the platform; deep ecology has no position on diaspora policy.

culture-before-state.rationale: Not addressed in the platform; it calls for deep cultural and ideological change but gives no sequence relative to state-building.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed in the platform; deep ecology is mostly neutral on theology, and adherents differ.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed in the platform; deep ecology is not a feminist doctrine and its scope excludes ecofeminism.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Inferred from Naess's demand for non-exploitative relations between groups, which tells against ethnic economic dominance.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Not addressed in the platform; the call for local autonomy gives no answer on merging regions.

independent-unions.rationale: Deep ecology is silent on labour organisation; its platform concerns ecological and cultural change, not unions.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Not addressed; Naess opposed class exploitation but the platform has no view on what makes a society socialist.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Not addressed; the emphasis on local autonomy suggests local control but the platform names no particular services.

second-chamber.rationale: The platform says nothing on legislative design.

municipal-property.rationale: Naess's platform favours local autonomy and decentralisation, but no ownership model is stated; adherents range widely.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Local autonomy and bioregional ideas fit confederal structures, but the platform does not discuss institutional design.

family-wage.rationale: Not addressed; the platform's call for quality of life over standard of living gives no direction on wages.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not addressed; adherents' scepticism of technological fixes suggests caution, but deep ecology has no view on drug regulation.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from the platform's call for a gradual fall in human population and acceptance of natural life cycles; extending lifespans cuts against that spirit.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Not addressed; the platform has no view on money or state control of payments.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not addressed; no stated position on online identity.

person-over-state.rationale: Deep ecology is biocentric and holds that humans are part of a larger whole; this rejects human-centred framing, so a strongly person-centred state view is not its own. Inferred from the relational total-field view.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Naess's Self-realisation and deep-seated life values emphasise spiritual and non-material fulfilment, though the platform is not religious; inferred.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Not addressed; the platform favours local autonomy but does not discuss the constitutional status of regional powers.

gm-crops.rationale: Inferred from deep ecology's suspicion of technological manipulation of nature and its demand for non-exploitative approaches.

dense-cities.rationale: Inferred from the platform's aim to reduce human impact and population pressure, which favours compact settlement and less sprawl into wild land.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Naess's platform opposes exploitation between groups and the ideology is universalist about value; racial group politics conflicts with its biocentric egalitarianism.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from its universalist stance; the platform concerns value of all life and does not promote group pride.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Not addressed; Earth First! style direct action targets ecological harm, not state wars, so the tradition's non-exploitative principle suggests defensive-only force.

language-defines-nation.rationale: The platform is silent on nations, and Naess's bioregional local autonomy points away from language-defined nations without condemning them.

communal-electorates.rationale: Deep ecology has no stated position on religious electorates and treats the issue as outside its platform.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: The platform has no geopolitical content; an inference from its anti-exploitation and cross-group non-exploitation stance is mild scepticism of national-plot narratives.

free-public-college.rationale: The platform says nothing on tuition and the movement is not organised around education policy.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Deep ecologists call for deep structural change in economic and technological structures, so a price on pollution as the main tool is inferred to be the shallow approach Naess contrasts with it.

future-generations.rationale: Deep ecology's call to protect the richness of life and reduce human interference with nature implies a duty to leave the Earth undamaged, though the platform does not name future generations explicitly.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Deep ecology is distinct from ecofeminism and its platform says nothing about gendered values.

arms-reduction.rationale: Naess's emphasis on non-exploitative relations and less interference with nature suggests support for lower armaments; inferred, not stated.

open-diplomacy.rationale: The platform does not address diplomacy, and the movement has no recognised position.

capital-controls.rationale: Naess's local autonomy and opposition to growth-driven economics imply support for limiting global capital flows; inferred, not stated.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The platform is silent on who may bear arms; its nonviolent, locally autonomous outlook gives no clear direction.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Nonviolence is part of the movement's direct-action ethic, so conscientious refusal of state wars is inferred as modestly favoured; war is not a platform topic.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Naess's anti-class posture opposes exploitation, but the platform says nothing about unions or bargaining.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Not addressed; the preference for quality of life over a higher standard of living gives no clear direction on income top-ups.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Not addressed; the movement rejects growth-driven economics but does not discuss borrowing limits.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Naess's anti-class posture extends to exploitation between nations, so fairer rules for poorer countries are inferred as favoured.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The movement favours gradual deep change and nonviolent action, and its green party 'realists' work within the state, so smashing it is inferred as disfavoured.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Naess stresses diversity and local autonomy, so freedom for communities to choose differing economic arrangements is inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: The platform holds that nonhuman life has value in itself, independent of human usefulness, so pricing nature as capital is rejected as shallow, though some adherents tolerate it tactically.

sacred-nation.rationale: Naess favours local and bioregional autonomy over large state loyalties, so a sacred nation is inferred as disfavoured.

student-debt-relief.rationale: The sources do not address this issue, so the answer is inferred from the general principles and adherents are split.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Not addressed, though local autonomy and non-exploitative relations between groups point mildly toward concern.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Deep ecology rejects human specialness yet also resists technological tampering; adherents are split and the sources do not address human nature directly.

public-service-media.rationale: Not addressed; local autonomy and soft technique give no clear stance on funded media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: The platform is deliberately pluralist, inviting many religious and philosophical total views to support it, so it neither asserts nor denies that religions share one truth; inferred.

farm-price-support.rationale: The platform says nothing on farm support; its call for local autonomy and non-exploitative relations cuts both ways on state price guarantees.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Not addressed directly; Naess's rejection of violence and of the industrial-technological path implies giving up nuclear arms, but adherents rarely discuss deterrence.

workers-own-party.rationale: Naess's view cuts across class and left-right lines and calls for an anti-class posture, so a separate workers' party is not its vehicle; inferred.

ban-fgm.rationale: The platform does not mention it; respect for all life and anti-exploitation attitudes imply opposition to the practice, though deep ecologists also stress respect for local cultures.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; Naess's anti-class stance against exploitation between groups implies equal treatment, inferred.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed; the platform's emphasis on diversity and local autonomy implies respecting each region's own name for its variety.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: The platform calls for deep structural and policy change, not case-by-case private suits, and pollution harms far more than one owner's property; inferred.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Not addressed; respect for indigenous and traditional communities and local autonomy pulls one way, the absence of any institutional programme the other.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Point 3 and the call for policy change say humans have no right to reduce diversity except for vital needs, so conflicting freedoms give way; the platform stresses human obligations to nature.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not addressed; the anti-class stance and nonviolent ethos suggest a preference for judicial discretion, inferred.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Not addressed; the emphasis on local cultural diversity cuts against requirements, while community integration cuts for them.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Deep ecology is a philosophy about nature and says nothing on union membership rules; adherents have no common view.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed by the platform; adherents have no common position on voter identification.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Inferred from the platform's pluralism and non-dominating stance and the inclusion of many religious and philosophical foundations for the movement.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Inferred: the platform values deep change in policies, and its supporters judge governments by their effect on the biosphere rather than by electoral procedure alone.

premarital-sex.rationale: The platform does not address sexual morality; adherents have no shared view.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the local autonomy and non-exploitative ethos of the platform; not addressed directly.

negative-income-tax.rationale: The platform is silent on welfare design; adherents have no common position.

women-suffrage.rationale: Inferred from Naess's emphasis on equal intrinsic worth and non-domination, which adherents would extend to equal rights for women; not stated in the sources.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: The platform names no cause of women's oppression and many adherents draw on religious traditions; inferred disagreement.

race-social-construct.rationale: Inferred from the platform's value of diversity and equal worth of beings; not discussed in the sources.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not addressed by the platform; adherents have no shared position on state gender-equality bodies.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Biospherical egalitarianism and intrinsic value of nature suggest humans cannot own nature by claiming it; inferred.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Deep ecology is a philosophy that says little on international justice.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: The platform is not tied to literal scripture and draws on varied spiritual traditions; inferred.

gendered-self-government.rationale: The platform says nothing on gender in self-government; adherents split.

defend-planned-state.rationale: The platform rejects industrial civilization and the growth economy, so defending a planned industrial state is inferred as opposed.

indirect-election.rationale: Local autonomy is favoured but the sources do not address indirect selection.

national-church-status.rationale: Deep ecology's anti-class, non-exploitative posture suggests no privileged legal status for a church; inferred.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Naess's local autonomy and non-exploitative relations between groups suggest support for minority autonomy; inferred.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Local autonomy suggests inhabitants should decide; inferred.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Bioregionalism organises places by natural regions, so inherited colonial borders are inferred as arbitrary.

simple-living.rationale: The platform asks for quality of life over a rising standard of living and Naess favoured simple means, rich ends.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Local autonomy and protection of native ways of life suggest support; inferred.

equal-conscription.rationale: The platform says nothing on conscription; adherents split.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Inferred from the movement's reverence for place and bioregional attachment; the platform does not frame it as a national duty.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Inferred: the platform's respect for all life and non-exploitative relations makes killing without trial unthinkable.

close-ties-china.rationale: The philosophy does not address foreign alignment, and adherents are indifferent to it.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on local autonomy and non-exploitative relations between groups, not national kinship.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Not addressed; adherents are indifferent on tax design.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Not addressed by the platform; no stated stance on social programme design.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred from the stress on local autonomy and grassroots action, which opposes leader-centred politics.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Inferred from the platform's concern for non-exploitative relations; the question is not addressed.

national-resource-control.rationale: Not addressed; deep ecology favours local and bioregional control but not nation-state control as such.

distribution-by-process.rationale: The platform is about ecological limits and non-exploitation between groups, not entitlement theory; adherents are indifferent, inferred from the platform's silence.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: The platform's concern is non-exploitative relations between groups in general; it takes no stand on race, so this is left neutral.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from the platform's preference for quality of life over a rising standard of living and its critique of technological growth structures.

multipolar-world.rationale: Inferred from the platform's call for local autonomy and decentralisation, which opposes one dominant power.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The platform locates value in nature itself and says nothing about labour as the source of the value of goods.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from the platform's stress on place, bioregion and the whole biosphere over national loyalty, and its anti-class framing.

material-over-identity.rationale: The platform addresses neither left strategy nor identity politics, and its focus on non-material quality of life cuts both ways.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from the platform's opposition to growth-driven industrial economies and its call for local autonomy over party-led direction.

missingStatements.text: Humans have no right to reduce the diversity of life except to satisfy vital needs.
missingStatements.rationale: Point three of the platform states this directly.

missingStatements.text: A society should aim for quality of life rather than a rising standard of living.
missingStatements.rationale: Point seven of the platform asks for this shift in economic goals.

missingStatements.text: Human beings should be understood as part of nature rather than as separate from or above it.
missingStatements.rationale: Naess's relational total-field view rejects the man-in-environment image and treats organisms as knots in a biospherical net.

notes: Many answers are inferences because deep ecology is a value platform without a program on most political questions, so few statements are stated positions. Some adherents link it to green anarchism, others (Naess) engaged with green parties; Earth First! style activists differ from Naess on tactics.
